fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(18, 14))

# --- Plot 1: Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex ---
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sns.barplot(data=df, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', ax=ax1, palette='viridis', ci=None)

ax1.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=14)

                 textcoords='offset points')

# --- Plot 2: Age Distribution by Survival Status ---
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
sns.histplot(data=df, x='age', hue='survived', multiple='stack', kde=True, ax=ax2, palette='magma', bins=30)
ax2.set_title('Age Distribution by Survival Status', fontsize=18, weight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=14)
ax2.set_ylabel('Number of Passengers', fontsize=14)
legend = ax2.get_legend()
legend.set_title('Status')
legend.get_texts()[0].set_text('Did Not Survive')
legend.get_texts()[1].set_text('Survived')

# --- Plot 3: Fare Distribution by Survival Status ---
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
sns.boxenplot(data=df, x='survived', y='fare', ax=ax3, palette='plasma')
ax3.set_title('Fare Distribution by Survival Status', fontsize=18, weight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Survival Status', fontsize=14)
ax3.set_ylabel('Fare (Log Scale)', fontsize=14)
ax3.set_xticklabels(['Did Not Survive', 'Survived'])
# Use a log scale due to the extreme skewness of the 'fare' data
ax3.set_yscale('log')
ax3.set_ylim(bottom=1) # Avoid log(0) issues for fares of 0

# --- Plot 4: Survival Rate by Family Size ---
df['family_size'] = df['sibsp'] + df['parch']

ax4.set_xlabel('Number of Family Members Aboard', fontsize=14)
ax4.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=14)
ax4.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.97])
